newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus stock exchange hits new low.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus stock exchange hits new low.

text.p: Cyprus's exchange fell to a new low of 77.45 on Wednesday, losing 1.16 percent in one day and 2.78 percent since Friday.

The 41-share Cyprus Stock Exchange (CSE) all-share index, set at 100 points, lost 1.45 percent on Tuesday and another 1.16 percent on Wednesday. Shares on the market have been registering declines since the beginning of the year.

Analysts have attributed the fall in part by renewed tension with Turkey, which has occupied a third of the island since a 1974 invasion sparked by a brief coup engineered by the military regime then ruling in Greece.
Others have said the fall was sparked by the need for extra cash to cover heavy buying registered on the bourse on Monday.
"A sharp shock to the market will probably help it recover," one senior trader told Reuters. "Suddenly people will realise that life moves on irrelevant to the political situation."
CSE director Nondas Metaxas told Reuters earlier Wednesday he expected the government to announce incentives for investments in the exchange in the next two to three days.

Losses have been registered in all seven sub-indices since Friday. On Wednesday insurance, tourist businesses and miscellaneous companies showed they were bucking the trend with increases ranging from 0.03 percent to 1.36 percent.
Banking stocks closed at 87.10, down 2.94 percent from Friday's close of 89.74. Shares of the Bank of Cyprus retreated 11 cents to close at 324.5. Popular Bank shares closed at 316, down 9 cents.
The Hellenic Bank closed at 255.5, down 3.5 cents. The Universal Savings Bank dropped one cent, closing at 136.5.
Approved Investment stocks closed at 69.12, down 4.31 percent from Friday. Insurance corporations closed at 56.17, up from 56.05 recorded last week.
Universal Life insurance made gains of 18.5 cents to close at 391. Paneuropean Insurance closed down one cent, at 113.5. Interamerican lost 2.5 cents, closing at 99.
Cement producer Vassiliko closed down 8.5 cents to 144.5. Beer and wine producer Keo closed the day at 108.5, down two cents from Friday.
